content:
Subject: Inbox Cleanup Request

Hi Assistant,

Could you please help me clean up the notification clutter in my inbox? Specifically, I would like to remove emails from automated and security senders. 

Thank you!

Best,  
[Your Name]

I can do that. Quick question before I start:

1) Do you want me to permanently delete those emails (move to Trash), or just archive/move them out of the inbox (e.g., to All Mail or an Archive folder/label)?  
2) Are there any senders or keywords I should definitely preserve (e.g., security@company.com, important alerts from services you rely on), or should I treat all automated/notification/security-type messages as removable?

If you’re okay with me choosing a conservative default, I can: search the Inbox and Sent for messages matching common automated/security patterns (senders containing "no-reply", "noreply", "do-not-reply", "notifications@", "notification@", "alert@", "security@", and subjects containing "notification", "alert", "verification", "receipt", "digest"), show you a short summary (counts and top senders), then proceed to either archive or delete them based on your answer. Which do you prefer?
Please archive them and preserve any emails from security@company.com. Thank you!

I couldn't find any messages in the Inbox that match the automated/notification keywords I tried. Before I proceed, could you confirm how you'd like me to continue?

Options:
1) Search All Mail (and Archive any matches) — this will find automated/notification emails that may already be archived or labeled elsewhere. I will preserve any from security@company.com as you requested.  
2) Search additional folders (Promotions, Updates, Spam, Sent) instead of All Mail.  
3) If you prefer, I can run a stricter or looser keyword/sender search — tell me any extra senders or keywords to include or exclude.

Which option do you want? If you pick 1 or 2, I’ll run the search and then archive the matched messages (move them out of the Inbox) while preserving emails from security@company.com.
Option 1 is fine. Please search All Mail and archive any matches while preserving emails from security@company.com. Thank you!

I ran a broad keyword search across All Mail for common automated/notification terms but it returned no matches. That means none of your messages matched the patterns I used.

Two safe options to continue — please pick one:

1) Broaden the criteria by archiving any messages in All Mail older than a certain age (suggestion: 90 days). I will skip any from security@company.com. This captures older notifications that likely aren’t needed.  
2) I can run additional searches by sender patterns or specific services (examples: senders containing "no-reply", "noreply", "notifications", "mailer", "updates@", or service names like "github", "slack", "jira", "aws", "google", etc.). Tell me any services or extra keywords to include or I can pick a comprehensive list and show you a summary before archiving.

Which would you like? If you choose option 1, tell me the age threshold (e.g., 90 days). If you choose option 2, list any senders/services to target or say “use a comprehensive list” and I’ll proceed and show counts/top senders before archiving.
I choose option 1 with the age threshold of 90 days. Please proceed. [END]
